argmax.description: One accepted router selection, repeated at every token in the original interleaved execution order. Input0 is a contiguous CUDA float32[8] view of the actual produced softmax row. Initialize from expert 0, then scan experts 1 through 7 with strict probability > selected_probability; never replace equality, preserving first-expert ties and ordered floating comparison behavior. Return the complete selection tuple: 0 rank-zero int32 selected expert, 1 rank-zero float32 selected probability copied without numerical conversion. The unchanged full softmax and latest routing state remain live through explicit schedule bindings; they are not recomputed or mutated by selection. This separate argmax proof target does not imply that approximately related upstream score vectors select the same expert.

capacity_routing.description: One serial accepted selected-weight/capacity/routing update, with all loop-carried live state explicit. Inputs, contiguous on one CUDA device: input0 rank-zero int32 selected expert in [0,8); input1 rank-zero float32 selected probability; input2 int64[8] prefix counts before this token; input3 int64[8,32] full initialized token table; input4 float32[8,32] full initialized combine-weight table; input5 int32[input6,8] previously written survival rows; input6 is the token position in [0,256). State must be reachable after exactly input6 preceding accepted token updates. Preserve the original __fdiv_rn(p,p), even for dropped tokens, without replacing it by 1; use the original int64 postincrement rank, expert-order survival comparisons and rank < 32 capacity drop, retaining demand for drops. Return fresh complete state with one dtype and meaning per slot at every occurrence: 0 int64[8] updated prefix, including at token 255; 1 int64[8,32] full token table; 2 float32[8,32] full combine table; 3 int32[input6+1,8] complete written survival prefix. Only the number of live survival rows grows; its dtype and meaning never change. Future unwritten rows are not live and are neither read nor padded. The existing final demand conversion is a separate expert_demand family so this family's output ABI is independent of token position. No earlier demand conversions, input-alias mutations or hidden state are introduced.

expert_demand.description: The accepted router_capacity kernel's existing final expert-order int64-to-int32 demand conversion, extracted at the real boundary after token 255. Input0 is contiguous CUDA int64[8] prefix counts produced by all 256 routing updates, including capacity-dropped tokens; each count is in [0,256] and the total is 256. Execute the original serial loop over experts 0 through 7 and int32_t(prefix[expert]) conversion exactly once. Return output 0 as fresh int32[8] expert_demand with a fixed dtype and meaning. Full token indices, combine probabilities and written survival rows bypass this operation through explicit final-output bindings and are not mutated. This semantic split keeps routing prefix counts and final demand distinct for proof setup; it extracts existing arithmetic, not an invented epilogue.

projection_softmax.description: Accepted fixed-layout router projection and softmax, followed by the original capacity-state initialization up to the real boundary before token 0. Preconditions: contiguous same-device CUDA bfloat16 input0 [256,512] tokens and input1 [512,8] runtime router weights, with the accepted softmax_exp domain. Serial token/expert/hidden loops, ascending 512-term __fmaf_rn dot products, original fmaxf scan, scalar SLEEF exponential with all original hexadecimal constants and explicit rounding, ascending denominator additions, __fdiv_rn and __fmul_rn are retained; there are no tensor-core instructions in this variant. Outputs: 0 softmax float32[256,8]; 1 initial prefix int64[8]; 2 initialized token_indices int64[8,32]; 3 initialized combine probabilities float32[8,32]; 4 live survival prefix int32[0,8]. Scores are internal and dead after softmax. The empty survival prefix represents no initialized rows, not zero-filled future rows. Initialization is existing accepted work, not an invented prologue. All outputs have fresh storage; neither input is mutated.
